subject: Google AI Promotional Licence Programme
body:
Dear Sir/ Ma'am,

Here’s your final call to turn your ideas into innovation! Don’t miss the
opportunity to explore the power of AI.
*Registrations are open on a first-come, first-served basis and will close
as soon as the available licences are filled.*

Submit your ideas now and take the first step towards making them a reality!

Survey Form Link
<https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScFuR_mN16jr54SA9W0sJHC4XI7Kk3nWBukmFuhRcNP3zrfIg/viewform?usp=sharing&ouid=114393717339172203576>

——— Earlier message ———

Dear Sir/Mam

We are embarking on an exciting initiative to bring the power of advanced
AI capabilities to a select group of students, faculty members and
administrative staff through a *Google AI Promotional Licence Programme*.

This is more than an opportunity to access cutting edge AI tools, it is
an opportunity to be among the early adopters and innovators who will
explore what AI can make possible, push the boundaries of existing
practices, and demonstrate its potential to create meaningful impact across
the University.

*What could you do with AI?*

We are looking for people with ideas and the ambition to put them into
action.

- *For Faculty:* Reimagine teaching and learning, create more engaging
academic experiences, explore new research possibilities and generate
knowledge in new ways.
- *For Students:* Deepen your understanding, develop new skills, tackle
challenging problems, build projects and turn ideas into reality.
- *For Administrative Staff:* Rethink routine processes, improve
reporting and decision-making, simplify workflows and explore opportunities
for intelligent automation.

Google will provide customised AI capabilities and connectors based on
the participant's role and area of application, helping selected
individuals access tools relevant to what they intend to accomplish.

*Who should apply?*

We are looking for individuals who are curious, proactive and willing to
experiment. You do not need to be an AI expert or an experienced user of AI
tools since Google will provide us with all the required training
needed. What matters is your ability to identify an opportunity, think
creatively about how AI could help, and demonstrate a genuine commitment to
putting it into practice.

*How will participants be selected?*

As the programme has a limited number of licences, participation will be
selected based on your Idea's potential. Applications will be evaluated on
the relevance and quality of the proposed ideas, their potential impact,
feasibility and the clarity of the expected outcomes.

*Take the first step*

If you have an idea worth exploring, a process worth rethinking, a
problem worth solving or simply the ambition to discover what AI can help
you achieve, we encourage you to participate.

Survey Form Link <https://forms.gle/CUfcxkfSNsLKTJrc7>

We look forward to seeing what you can create!

subject: Requirement for NAAC accreditation: Academic Programmes with Project Work, Internship, Fieldwork and Apprenticeship credited in the curriculum (Batches 2021 to 2026)
body:
Dear Madam / Sir,

As required for NAAC accreditation, it is necessary to identify all the
academic programmes in which *Project Work, Internship, Fieldwork, and
Apprenticeship* are included and credited as part of the curriculum.

Accordingly, the concerned *HoDs *and *Programme Heads* are requested to
furnish the details programme-wise offered from* 2021 batch to 2026
batch *across
the four designated categories (Project Work, Internship, Fieldwork, and
Apprenticeship).

Please provide the following particulars in the corresponding sub-columns,
using the enclosed Excel template separately for each batch:
   *Credit allotted:* Number of academic credits assigned in the curriculum
   scheme. (If direct standalone credits are not allotted to an
   internship/fieldwork, but the component forms part of the Continuous
   Assessment for a specific course, please enter as Integrated with CA)
   *Duration (in months):* Duration of the component (in months)
   *Semester/s:* Relevant Semester or Semesters
   *Number of Students:* Total number of students participating/enrolled in
   the component for the batch

The links to *supporting documentary proof* must be provided in the final
column of the Excel sheet (*Supporting Documents*), compiled in
coordination with the Industry-Interface Cell or other concerned
academic/administrative units.

Applicable documents include:
   Approved Course Matrix / Programme Structure
   Course Syllabus & Scheme of Evaluation
   Academic Regulations & Course Catalogues
   Internship / Apprenticeship references
   Project Work / Fieldwork Guidelines & Evaluation Rubrics
   Continuous Assessment Marks Records & Evaluation Patterns/Rubrics
   Industry Collaboration MOUs
   Student Allocation Letters & List of Students with Enrollment Numbers
   (where applicable)

*The consolidated data is required to be submitted to IQAC for fulfilling
the NAAC accreditation requirements.*

You are requested to submit the duly filled-in Excel sheet on or
before *November
30, 2026*.

subject: Syllabus revision comparative table for AQAR 2025-26 – IMPORTANT
body:
Dear Sir/Mam,

As a follow-up to our earlier communication, please note that 6th November
2026 is the timeline for submitting the syllabus revision comparative table
for AY 2025–26.

Kindly prioritise this submission to enable timely consolidation and
further evaluation.

——— Earlier message ———

Dear Sir /
Madam,

*At the outset, we extend our sincere appreciation for your cooperation
and contribution towards the successful submission of the Annual Quality
Assurance Report (AQAR) 2024. *

As you are aware, submission of the AQAR is a mandatory annual
requirement. We are now in the process of preparing the AQAR for the AY
2025–26. In this regard, it is essential to document and report the extent
of syllabus revisions undertaken during this academic year.

To meet NAAC documentation standards, all programmes that fall within the
revision cycle for AY 2025–26 must prepare a syllabus revision comparative
table using the prescribed format provided herewith.

*Please consider the following points while conducting syllabus revision
comparison :*

1. Syllabus revision comparison must be done for the 2025 batch with
the previously revised syllabus of a batch as per revision cycle for all
semesters. *Please note, revision cycle is considered UG – once in 4
years, and PG programmes – once in 2 years.*

2. A sample specimen format is enclosed that provides a breakdown of
the percentage of changes carried out in each course, module-wise and
average percentage for a programme considering all courses. *Please
maintain the same fonts, font size and format provided in the sample.*

3. A course is considered to have undergone a *syllabus change* if *20%
or more* of its content has been revised.

4. Syllabus of the latest revised batch (i.e. of 2025 batch) is to be
shown in the right-hand side column of the format. On the left-hand side,
the previous revised syllabus of the same subject should be compared
module-wise. Average should be calculated for a given course considering
all modules.

5. Change in teaching hours will not be considered as change in
syllabus. Rearrangements made in Modules / Courses between semesters will
not lead to change in syllabus. Renaming / minor changes in the course
content cannot be considered.

6. Courses with completely new syllabi across all modules should be
recorded as 100% change.

7. Consolidate all specialisations of AICTE ambit programme into a
single document by listing courses revised semesters-wise and then
calculate the average percentage of change in syllabus for all
specializations.*(enclosed sample documents for AICTE (BBA) and UGC
(Bcom) for reference)*

8. The respective Programme Heads / Coordinators and IQAC Coordinators
must ensure the quality and contents of the document as per standard format
before submitting.

*9. **The final document needs to be duly signed by both the Head of
the Department and Director / Deputy Director of the School before
submission. ** As the document will be submitted to IQAC for further
evaluation, all details must be thoroughly reviewed and duly validated
prior to submission.*

*Kindly submit your inputs** positively before November 6th, 2026.*

Thank you for your cooperation.

Regards,

subject: Invitation: JAIN x BluWheelz Interactive Session on EVpreneurship
body:
Dear Sir/Mam

Greetings!

JAIN (Deemed-to-be University) is pleased to share that the University is
collaborating with BluWheelz, India's fastest-growing EV logistics
platform. Built on an innovative Fleet-as-a-Service model, BluWheelz
specialises in first, mid, and last-mile deliveries, combining
capital-efficient operations, deep EV ecosystem partnerships and
cutting-edge retrofitting to enable cost-effective, zero-emission logistics
at scale.

BluWheelz's mission is to decarbonise India's logistics industry by
building a capital-light, technology-driven EV ecosystem focused on
4-wheeler fleet electrification. It does this by:
   Replacing diesel fleets with electric ones through strategic
   retrofitting and EV partnerships.
   Integrating OEMs, charge point operators, financing models and manpower
   partners into one unified logistics platform.

Through this collaboration, students, faculty and alumni will have the
opportunity to become entrepreneurs in this futuristic and eco-friendly EV
initiative under the *1,008 EVpreneurship Programme*.

To inaugurate this partnership and introduce the programme, an interactive
session has been organised with *Dr. Chenraj Roychand, Hon'ble Chancellor,

BluWheelz.*

body:
Dear Sir/Ma’am,

Greetings!

This is with reference to the earlier communication regarding the conduct
of Board of Studies (BoS) meetings for Academic Year 2027–28.

*Please note the revised timelines for conducting the BoS:*
   *UG Programmes:* On or before 30th November 2026
   *PG Programmes:* On or before 31st January 2027

*Kindly note that if PG programmes are adequately prepared, BoS meetings
for both UG and PG programmes may be conducted simultaneously on or before
30th November 2026.*

*Further, all HoDs are requested to fill in the Google Form and update the
proposed BoS meeting date and time for your respective departments using
the link provided below by 24th October,EOD.*

*Google Form Link :* BOS for AY 2027-28 (Schedule)
<https://forms.gle/QyPj73vc7fSgPXN77>

All Departments are requested to plan and complete the BoS within the
revised timelines. The standardised templates, formats, detailed checklist,
and other supporting documents required for the BoS process will be shared
with all Departments shortly.

——— Earlier message ———

Dear Sir/Ma'am,

Greetings!

As we progress through Academic Year 2026–27, it is important that our
academic programmes and curricula continue to remain relevant,
contemporary, and responsive to the evolving needs of learners, industry,
society, and the regulatory landscape. The Board of Studies (BoS) serves as
a key academic forum for Departments to critically review their academic
offerings and plan meaningful curricular interventions for the forthcoming
academic cycle.

*Accordingly, all Departments are requested to initiate and conduct their
Board of Studies (BoS) for AY 2027–28, with a forward-looking approach
towards strengthening the academic portfolio.*

*Board of Studies (BoS) for AY 2027–28*

*All Departments are required to conduct and complete the BoS for AY
2027–28 on or before 15th November 2026. *

Departments are requested to plan the activities leading up to the BoS
well in advance, particularly where inputs, consultations, external
expertise, or prior-level reviews are involved. Preparatory work may
include a review of existing programmes and courses, proposed curriculum
revisions, new programme initiatives, and opportunities for combined or
interdisciplinary programmes and courses.

Where new programme proposals or significant academic changes are under
consideration, Departments are requested to initiate the process at the
earliest, as these may require completion of the prescribed review stages
including consideration by the *Screening Committee* and *Standing
Committee* prior to placement before the BoS.

*BoS Document Readiness*

To support a systematic and consistent BoS process across Departments, the
framework below may be used as a reference for document readiness.
Departments are requested to ensure that the relevant documents and
supporting evidence are updated and maintained accordingly.

*Category*

*Documents / Evidence to be Maintained*

*Pre-BoS Inputs*

DPAC/DIAC Agenda & Minutes; Stakeholder Feedback – New Programmes;
Stakeholder Feedback – Curriculum; Benchmarking Documents

*Programme and Curriculum*

Programme Overview; Programme Structure; Course Matrix; Course Syllabus;
Course Revision Log; Open Elective Basket; CO–PO/PSO Mapping; NEP/Other
Regulatory Compliances

*Department and BoS Composition*

Department Vision, Mission & Overview; BoS Composition; External Member
Profiles; Nomination/Consent Documents, wherever applicable

*New / Interdisciplinary Proposals*

New Programme Proposal; 1-Year PG Programme Proposal, wherever applicable;
Combined/Interdisciplinary Programme or Course Proposal; Academic Rationale
and Feasibility

*Preliminary Reviews*

Screening Committee / Standing Committee Presentations; Observations;
Recommendations; Action Taken, wherever applicable

*BoS Meeting*

BoS Notice & Agenda; BoS Presentation; Attendance; Minutes of Meeting;
Resolutions; Action Items

*Approval and Closure*

Required Approval Records; Final Approved Curriculum/Programme Documents;
Digitally Signed Documents; Version History; Consolidated Final BoS
Repository

*Departments are requested to ensure that documentation is complete and
supported by appropriate evidence. The standardised templates, formats, a
detailed checklist, and other supporting documents for the BoS process will

subject: Requirement || AQAR 2025-26 – Documentation of Courses: Employability / Entrepreneurship / Skill Development
body:
Dear Sir / Mam,

As part of the AQAR 2025–26 submission, we are also required to identify
and document courses that contribute to *Employability / Entrepreneurship /
Skill Development*. In addition, we must demonstrate how the curricula are
aligned with *Local / National / Regional / Global* developmental needs, as
reflected in the Programme Outcomes (POs), Programme Specific Outcomes
(PSOs), and Course Outcomes (COs).

To ensure uniformity and completeness, kindly follow the instructions
below. Please also refer to the attached sample Word document
(25BBAFA1C01.docx) and Excel sheet (Course Activities.xlsx) for the
standard format.

1. *Courses to be Included*: All unique Courses (Theory / Lab / Project)
offered during AY 2025-26 that are directly leading to Employability /
Entrepreneurship / Skill Development are to be considered from respective
programmes of following batches :

· 2025 batch: Semesters 1 & 2

· 2024 batch: Semesters 3 & 4

· 2023 batch: Semesters 5 & 6

· 2022 batch: Semesters 7 & 8

2. *Word File Preparation (One File per Course)*: The course document in
a Word File should have all the relevant contents, namely, Course Code,
Course Name, Credits / teaching hours, Objectives, Course Outcomes (COs),
Modules with hour’s distribution and References.

3. *Formatting requirements*:

· Use colour-coded combination for highlighting the Course Contents
/ Modules and Course Outcomes as per the sample attached
“25BBAFA1C01.docx”. So that the course document provides appropriate
mapping of its contents to Employability / Entrepreneurship / Skill
Development.

· Common courses offered by a Department / School in their
respective programmes need to be considered only once.

· The Header and Footer of Word Document should be retained
commonly for all courses as per the sample, also A4 size alignment, fonts
and font size.

· Each Course should be documented in a separate Word File. The
File Name of the Word Document has to be given with the respective Course
Code.
For Eg : “25BBAFA1C01.docx”.

· Please ensure that there are no extra characters / spaces occur
in the File Name.

· Please note that course code should be obtained from the Approved
Curriculum Matrix from the ERP System.

4. *Excel Sheet Compilation:* The Courses which are being documented as
per the above requirements are also needed to be listed in a tabular
format, preferably in a single Excel Sheet (attached – “Course
Activities.xlsx”), consisting the following columns :

*Column*

*Description*

*I. **Course Code (Unique)*

Unique Code of the Course offered during AY 2025-26 (Eg: 25BBAFA1C01)

*II. **Name of the Course*

Course Name should be provided (Eg. Financial Accounting)

*III. **Year of Introduction*

Year of Course introduced / revised. (Eg: 2025 / 2024 / 2023)

*IV. **Activities / Content with direct bearing on Employability /
Entrepreneurship / Skill Development*

Please provide a write up with 25 to 30 Words

*V. **Course offered by the Programme with Specialisation*

Name of the Programme with Specialisation. (Eg. Bachelor of Science in
Forensic Science)

*VI. **Semester*

Semester which the course was offered during the AY 2025-26

*VII. **Batch*

Batch of the respective programme offering respective course during the AY
2025-26. (Eg: 2025 batch / 2024 batch)

*VIII. **“New” Course introduced during AY 2025-26*

Mark as “New” if revised or introduced in AY 2025–26, else “Old”

*IX. **Link to the Course document*

Hyperlink can be generated that directs to a Word file with the extension
.docx, which is stored in the same folder along the Excel file. This
hyperlink can then be tested to ensure it opens the linked Word file
successfully.

*X. **Relevance of Curriculum to Local Developmental Needs*

Mark as “Yes” if curriculum has relevance to Local Developmental Needs,
else “No”

*XI. **Relevance of Curriculum to Regional Developmental Needs*

Mark as “Yes” if curriculum has relevance to Regional Developmental Needs,
else “No”

*XII. **Relevance of Curriculum to National Developmental Needs*

Mark as “Yes” if curriculum has relevance to National Developmental Needs,
else “No”

*XIII. **Relevance of Curriculum to Global Developmental Needs*

Mark as “Yes” if curriculum has relevance to Global Developmental Needs,
else “No”

*Important Note: *

· Courses should be considered as ‘NEW’ only if they are newly
introduced or substantial changes made in the course contents during the AY
2025-26.

· Year of Introduction shall be 2025 for new / revised courses
introduced during AY 2025-26.

· Please avoid indicating a course as New, if there is only change
made in title of the course without changes in the course contents.

· Courses marked as relevant to Local, Regional, National, or
Global developmental needs must also reflect this alignment in the
corresponding POs, PSOs, and COs. A separate follow-up on this will be
conducted after your submission.

5. *Folder preparation:* The respective Department or the School must
document all the Courses in a single Excel Sheet and all the Word files in
a single Folder in order to ensure only UNIQUE COURSES are consolidated, as
per sample zipped folder attached “Folder Sample - Department of Food
Technology.zip”.

*The respective Programme Heads, Programme Coordinators and IQAC
Coordinators must ensure the quality and contents of the document as per
standard format before submitting. As the document will be submitted to
IQAC for further evaluation, all details must be thoroughly reviewed and
duly validated prior to submission.*

*Please send the furnished Course Documents in Word Format and the
Tabulation of Activities of all Courses in One Excel sheet, as required in
a single Folder, for all programmes with specialization offered during AY
2025-26 at Department / School level. **The consolidated folder may kindly
be submitted on or before 21st September 2026, by 1:00 PM.*

subject: New Program Proposal Submission – 2027-28
body:
Dear Sir/ Ma'am,
Greetings.

As we prepare for the Academic Year *2027–28*, the University invites
Departments to submit proposals for *New Academic Programmes* that align
with emerging trends, evolving industry requirements, and the institutional
vision of academic excellence.

New programme proposals are expected to strategically respond to the *evolving
demands of the 21st-century landscape*, with due consideration to
*marketability,
profitability, employability, sustainability, innovation, and contemporary
relevance*. Departments are encouraged to explore programmes that move
beyond traditional disciplinary boundaries and incorporate *interdisciplinary
approaches, digital literacy, critical thinking, adaptive problem-solving,
entrepreneurship, and internationalisation*.

The proposed programmes may also focus on *emerging industries, evolving
societal needs, and future-oriented areas*, while contributing to the
effective implementation of the *National Education Policy (NEP) 2020*. The
objective is to develop *future-proof academic programmes* that address
current requirements while anticipating emerging trends and ensuring
continuous relevance and innovation.

Departments are requested to submit proposals for *new UG, PG, and 1-year
PG programmes* by *7th September 2026.*

All proposals will undergo an initial *Screening Committee* process before
being placed for further discussion before the *Standing Committee and
Board of Studies (BoS)*.

Kindly submit the detailed programme proposal through the Google Form
provided below:

*Please find the Submission Link here: New Programme Proposal Submission
Form
<https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdyI2tETN1r3shq986rMVxdIWZKaWQkdZDoG093xVciSr12GA/viewform?usp=sharing&ouid=114393717339172203576>*

For any clarifications or guidance regarding the proposal, Departments may
reach out during *Office Hours on Thursday at 3.00 pm or* contact the *Office
of Academics* directly.

We look forward to the active participation of all Departments in
strengthening and shaping the University's academic portfolio through
innovative, relevant, and future-ready programmes.
